title: Retention curves, churn and customer value over time

videos.script: A cohort table is honest and hard to read. Eighteen rows of numbers do not make anybody decide anything. {{table}} A retention curve does. Take each cohort's row, draw it as a line falling from one hundred per cent, and put lines next to each other. Where they part, something is different. {{curve}} At Panela, customers who arrived through a friend's referral are still ordering a year later four times as often as customers who came from social media. {{channels}} And the cohorts of 2025 hold on better than the cohorts of 2024, from the third month on. Something changed in January, and the curves show when. {{better}} Two more numbers come out of the same data. Churn, which needs a definition before it means anything. And customer value, the money a customer brings in over time, which is the number that says how much it is worth paying to find one. {{value}} This lesson draws the curves, defines churn from the data rather than from a guess, and adds up what each channel's customers are worth. {{end}}
